annotations.title: Make a part from a description (Overwing CAD)

description: Makes a real CAD part from a description: a bracket, an enclosure, an adapter, a jig. Overwing writes a parametric script, builds it with a CAD kernel, measures it, checks it against what was asked, and stores a STEP file and STL files for 30 days. Costs 300 credits a part from the account's balance, charged when the job starts and given back if no part comes out. This tool answers at once with a job id; the part takes one to three minutes. Then call cad_get with the id about every 20 seconds until status is complete, and give the person part_url (a page that shows the part in 3D with download buttons, no account needed). Do not call cad_create again for the same part while a job is building. Pass idempotency_key, a string you make up for this part, so that a call that got no answer can be repeated: the same key with the same arguments returns the job already started and charges nothing more. To change a part made earlier, pass its job id as `from` and say in the prompt what should change. Give sizes in millimetres and say what the part mates with; anything left out is assumed and listed in the answer. Needs an organization key; with too few credits the answer says how the owner can add them.

from.description: An earlier job id of this account (cadj_...) or a part id (cadp_...): the new part starts from that one's script.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. A string you choose for this part (letters, digits, - _ . :), for example a UUID. A call repeated with the same key and the same arguments within 24 hours returns the job already started instead of starting and charging a second one. Use a new key for each new part.

params.description: With `from`: new values for the earlier part's named parameters, for example { "width": 80 }. Numbers, booleans or strings.

prompt.description: What to make, or with `from` what to change. Sizes in millimetres, hole sizes and positions, what it mates with, how it will be made (printed, machined).
